label: Spiritual, weakest reading: not composed of matter and form
definition: IsSpiritual MatterForm g: g is not composed of matter and form (¬ MatterForm g; ST I q.3 a.2). Example: an angel on the Thomist account; counterexample: an animal. With RemoteFromAll (entering into the composition of nothing) it is the altogether-immaterial antecedent of the q.14 a.1 intellect premise (DEF-ALTOGETHER-IMMATERIAL).
note: Analyst reading of Dei Filius ch. 1's 'substantia spiritualis', attribution deferred. 'Substance' (subsisting rather than inhering in another) is not typed; the root endpoint's represented esse/essence identity is stronger than 'substance' and is not used for this conjunct. Incorporeal-but-composite readings are not separated here. On its own IsSpiritual is also satisfied by prime matter and by accidents (neither is composed of matter and form); only the RemoteFromAll conjunct of the Dei Filius attributes excludes them jointly.
